subject: Post-call: SkipWave ops & model-fit recap
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@skipwave.com>, Daniel Park <dpark@skipwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SkipWave ops & model-fit recap

Hi Olivia / Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of customer goals / pain: 
- Primary goal: Serve real-time product-recommendations in the storefront (sub-300ms 95th latency for top-line API calls).
- Current pain: unpredictable tail latency during peak batch scoring (~3x spike at morning peak), tokenized models limiting throughput on their current VMs, and limited KV-cache for session affinity.
- Non-functional: data residency requirement for EU customers (we noted US first-phase, EU later), and strong emphasis on audit logs / request tracing for compliance.

Technical highlights we discussed: 
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 300ms for short-inference path (prompt length <= 128 tokens); P50 around 60–80ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 1,500 qps for batched ranking requests during peak; bursts to 3,000 qps expected during campaigns.
- Model family: please confirm if you plan to run a 7B autoregressive model (user-specified finetune) or a dual-stage architecture (7B ranking model + 33B generation fallback). Our recommendation at first pass is to qualify for a quantized 7B for primary low-latency route and a larger variant for fallbacks.
- Topology suggestion (initial): Dedicated inference pool in us-west for primary traffic, autoscale groups for burst capacity, and warm-standby region in eu-west for failover. KV caching at the serving layer for repeated prefixes; prefix-sharding by customer segment to minimize cold-KV penalties.

Attachments included: skipwave-deploy-topology-draft.pdf (sketch), slo-latency-throughput-sheet.xlsx (numbers & capacity model).

Immediate next steps / owners: 
1) SkipWave: confirm model choice (7B quantized vs. multi-tier) and expected token lengths for ranking vs. generation (owner: Olivia) — due EOD Thu 2028-04-05.
2) Redwood (Karthik): produce a deployment sketch with autoscale knobs and estimated GPU counts for steady-state & burst — deliverable by Fri 2028-04-06.
3) Naomi: schedule a focused deep-dive (1hr) on KV-caching and routing policies; proposed slot: Mon 2028-04-09 11:00 PT.

Open questions we flagged during call: 
- Data residency timeline for EU customers and whether EU requests must be served from eu-west only.
- Any hard constraints on encryption or additional logging retention beyond our standard 90-day default.

If that aligns, I will kick off the internal sizing and book the deep-dive.

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: SkipWave ops & model-fit recap

Adding a few technical clarifications from the engineering side based on today's notes.

Latency & sizing notes (short):
- The 300ms 95th SLO is achievable for a quantized 7B with careful batching (batch sizes ~8–12 for ranking) and prefix KV enabled. Expect P95 token generation cost ~180–220ms on a single A10G-equivalent instance when doing single-request path with small prompt lengths.
- For 1,500 sustained qps: recommend a hybrid pool with 8–10 GPUs in steady-state (batching + async workers); burst capacity via an autoscaler that can add +8 GPUs on <5min scale-up. Exact counts depend on observed prompt token distribution (please share histogram if available).

Model/architecture suggestions: 
- Primary (low-latency): quantized 7B, KV cache enabled, pinned to dedicated pool with small batching windows.
- Fallback (higher quality): 33B or sharded 16B, routed only when latency SLOs are relaxed (e.g., background re-rank or async enrichment).
- Routing policy: latency-first for customer-facing reads, cost-first for background batch jobs. We can provide a sample policy config in the next doc.

Deployment topology specifics: 
- Recommend regional pools + routing with weighted fallback. We'll design warm-standby in eu-west to honor data-residency once you confirm timeline.
- Observability: include token-level tracing and request-id propagation from front-end to serving runtime. Storage for KV caches should be colocated on serving nodes for microsecond access.

I attached the capacity sheet Naomi included and annotated the GPU sizing tab — see 'Estimates' worksheet.

Happy to walk through the math during the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

(Attachment: slo-latency-throughput-sheet.xlsx [annotated])

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@skipwave.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SkipWave ops & model-fit recap

Thanks Naomi and Karthik — this is helpful and mostly aligns with our internal thinking. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Model selection: we are leaning toward a 7B quantized model for the primary path. The fallback plan is a 33B tuned model for the weekly personalization jobs. We'll confirm token-length histograms by Thu.

2) Data residency: EU customers must have personal-data-affecting requests served from eu-west. However, anonymized batch re-training and analytics can be staged in US. We will share the compliance matrix with specific fields that cannot cross regions.

3) Encryption / logs: we need 12-month audit log retention for any user-identifiers used in request traces. Can Redwood provide a retention/archival plan that meets that?

Action: Olivia will share token-length histogram and compliance matrix by EOD Thu 2028-04-05. Once we have that, please proceed with sizing.

Olivia
Director of ML Engineering | SkipWave
olivia.chen@skipwave.com
